name: André Street
current_role: Co-founder of StoneCo (left board April 2024); angel/'late co-founder' investor in ~20 startups
profile: Brazilian fintech entrepreneur who sold his first payments company, Braspag, then co-founded StoneCo in 2012 with Eduardo Pontes; Stone broke the Cielo-Rede card-machine duopoly and IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2018. He left Stone's board in 2024 and now runs a personal VC operation (portfolio NAV ~US$200m) from the LTS (Lemann/Telles/Sicupira) office.
interesting_fact: Brazil Journal (Nov 2026) calls him probably Brazil's largest individual VC: ~40 startups backed incl. Brex, Cora, On Running and QI Tech; his Brex bet returned ~100x after he met its founders as teenagers when Stone bought Pagar.me.
deep_cut_fact: He says he personally took part in recruiting Stone's first 1,000 employees and for some years interviewed ~900 candidates a year; today he keeps mornings for sport and family and meets founders only 2pm-7pm.
notes: No longer at StoneCo management/board, so the Stone IR address is a weak route. His VC work runs out of the LTS family office in São Paulo; a warm intro via portfolio founders (e.g. QI Tech) is likely the best route. Some profiles also tie him to Teya (Europe), founded by Eduardo Pontes.

name: The Duke of Bedford
current_role: 15th Duke of Bedford (Andrew Russell); owner of the Woburn Estate and Bedford Estates (Bloomsbury, London)
profile: Andrew Russell (b. 1962), Harrow- and Harvard-educated, took over running Woburn Abbey from his parents in 2001 and succeeded as 15th Duke in 2003. Family wealth rests on the Woburn Estate in Bedfordshire and the Bedford Estates in Bloomsbury plus a major art collection; Sunday Times 2024 put it at ~£801m. Woburn Abbey has been closed since 2019 for a multi-year restoration.
interesting_fact: Woburn Abbey was founded in 1145 as a Cistercian monastery and granted to Sir John Russell (later 1st Earl of Bedford) in Henry VIII's will in 1547; the restoration has conserved all 24 of the Abbey's Canaletto paintings.
deep_cut_fact: The Woburn restoration involved 14,000 metres of scaffolding and lifting and re-laying 200,000 linear metres of floorboards; the gardens follow Humphry Repton's 1804 Red Book and are described as the most fully realised example of Repton's work.
notes: Private hereditary landowner, gives few interviews. Best route is the Woburn Abbey marketing team; woburn.co.uk also lists a Press Office page. Not an entrepreneurship/energy figure per se.

name: The Duke of Northumberland
current_role: 12th Duke of Northumberland (Ralph Percy); head of the Northumberland Estates
profile: Ralph Percy (b. 1956), Eton/Oxford-educated with a land-management degree from Reading, succeeded his brother as 12th Duke in 1995. Northumberland Estates manages ~100,000 acres and owns Alnwick Castle, Syon House (London) and Albury Park; Sunday Times 2024 estimated his wealth at £509m.
interesting_fact: He or the estate owns Alnwick, Warkworth and Prudhoe castles plus Syon House; Northumberland Estates has around 100 tenant farmers and directly manages 4,000 acres of forestry.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming Duke he spent seven years working in the Arundel Castle estate office, then returned north to manage the Alnwick estate for his elder brother, the 11th Duke.
notes: Energy angle: the estate began an ~£80k restoration of its 1889 River Aln hydroelectric scheme around 2010 (https://ghgenergy.blogspot.com/2011/03/landowners-fight-anglers-over.html?m=1, a secondary source) and has studied a heat network for Alnwick. Alnwick Castle also runs a podcast (podcast@alnwickcastle.com). Very private; go via the estate press office.

name: Ruan Hongxian
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Yixintang Pharmaceutical Group (一心堂, SZ:002727)
profile: Born 1966 in Mile, Yunnan, Ruan started trading medicinal herbs as a teenager, set up the Hongxiang herb-buying station in 1981, and founded the Yixintang drugstore chain (company formed 2000, first store 2001). Yixintang listed in Shenzhen in 2014 and now runs ~11,000 directly operated pharmacies across 10 provinces; with his daughters he controls ~31% of the company.
interesting_fact: Yixintang was the first directly operated drugstore chain to list on China's A-share market (Shenzhen, 2014); it has 11,000+ stores and 53m+ members. Ruan was also a torchbearer for the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
deep_cut_fact: His start: in 1980, on a trip from Mile to Kunming to sell sugarcane, he spotted a herb-buying notice, borrowed 40 kg of honeysuckle (jinyinhua) from his father, and made his first 100 yuan on the price gap; he says a childhood friend's death for lack of an 8-fen remedy drove him into medicine.
notes: Deep-cut source is a Chinese brand-profile aggregator (cnpp.cn) repeating the company's founding story; treat as company lore. Best route is the board secretary's office via the IR email (listed in the 2025 annual report summary, April 2026). Not an energy figure.

name: Kong Jinfeng
current_role: Director, Vice General Manager and Board Secretary, Delijia Transmission (德力佳传动, SSE:603092), Wuxi
profile: Kong Jinfeng and her husband Liu Jianguo (chairman/CTO) are the controlling shareholders of Delijia, a wind-turbine main-gearbox maker founded in Wuxi in January 2017; together they control ~42% via Nanjing Chenrui, a Wuxi employee partnership and direct stakes. Delijia listed on the Shanghai main board on 7 Nov 2025; wind OEMs Sany Renewable Energy and Envision are 5%+ shareholders and key customers.
interesting_fact: Delijia, founded only in 2017, makes main gearboxes for 2MW+ wind turbines and is building capacity for 1,000 large 8MW+ onshore gearboxes a year; media report it is top-3 globally and top-2 in China by share.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a billionaire co-founder, she personally serves as Delijia's board secretary, the officer named as the company's investor-relations contact in its 2025 listing announcement; she is also the managing partner of the Wuxi Detong staff shareholding partnership.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (wind-power drivetrain). Because she runs the board office, the IR email reaches her team directly. Her husband Liu Jianguo (chairman/CTO) gave a Shanghai Securities News interview at the IPO (paper.cnstock.com, 7 Nov 2025). Director term in the prospectus ran to June 2026; confirm she was re-appointed.

name: Wang Jun
current_role: Founder (and CEO per Wikipedia) of iCarbonX (碳云智能), Shenzhen/Zhuhai
profile: Genomics scientist (b. 1976) who in 1999, while a Peking University PhD student, founded BGI's bioinformatics group, later becoming BGI's CEO; his teams sequenced the first Asian genome, rice, SARS, the giant panda and the human gut microbiome. In 2015 he left BGI to found iCarbonX, an AI/multi-omics health company that now makes silicon-based biochips and works on drug discovery.
interesting_fact: iCarbonX raised over US$100m in its Series A within about six months of founding, valuing it near US$1bn; Wang described its goal as 'digitising life and longevity'. He presented iCarbonX at TED 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was named in Nature's 10 (2012) and Fortune's 40 under 40 (2013), won the 2005 Lundbeck Talent Prize, and held an Ole Rømer professorship at the University of Copenhagen.
notes: Input lists Chinese name 王军, but the BGI/iCarbonX founder is 王俊; profile assumes the iCarbonX founder (matches source_of_wealth). Fits a data/AI angle. iCarbonX also lists bd@icarbonx.com for business enquiries. Could not confirm his current title in 2026.

name: Fan Yi
current_role: Vice Chairman, General Manager (CEO) and legal representative, MLOptic Corp (茂莱光学, SSE STAR: 688502), Nanjing
profile: Fan Yi and his brother Fan Hao (chairman) are co-controllers of MLOptic, a Nanjing precision-optics maker founded in 1999; they control ~66% via Nanjing Maolai Holdings and direct stakes. The company grew from custom lenses and prisms into optical modules and inspection systems for semiconductors, life sciences, AR/VR and lidar, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023.
interesting_fact: MLOptic supplies lenses for China's domestic lithography machines (Shanghai Micro Electronics), microscope objectives to Israeli chip-inspection firm Camtek, inspection optics to KLA, and its space filters have flown on China's Ziyuan resource satellites.
notes: Low public profile; no personal bio or interviews found. Relevant to semiconductor/data-center supply chain (chip-inspection and lithography optics). Route via the board office IR email (2026 half-year report).

name: Jonathan Rowland
current_role: Financier/fintech entrepreneur; founder of R8 Capital and Mode (bitcoin app), co-founder of Redwood Bank (current titles unverified)
profile: Son of financier David Rowland, with whom he bought the good-bank remnant of Kaupthing Luxembourg via Blackfish Capital and launched Banque Havilland in 2009, serving as its CEO. He later co-founded UK challenger Redwood Bank and founded R8 Capital and Mode, an LSE-listed bitcoin and cashback app, as executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2020 his Mode Global Holdings said it would put up to 10% of its cash reserves into bitcoin, one of the first UK-listed companies to hold bitcoin as a treasury asset.
deep_cut_fact: In Feb 2021 Mode said it would host the original Bitcoin white paper on its website, the first UK-listed company to do so; Rowland said he hoped it would help others understand bitcoin's 'disruptive nature'.
notes: Wealth is shared with father David Rowland (Sunday Times listing). Banque Havilland lost its Luxembourg licence and is winding down (2024-25), and the family has had negative press around it; avoid in outreach. No personal published contact found; check Companies House for his current companies before outreach.

name: Chan Shirong
current_role: Director, Feng Tay Enterprises (豐泰企業, TWSE:9910), Douliu, Yunlin, Taiwan
profile: Chen Shih-jung (陳仕榮) is a long-serving board member and major individual shareholder (~38.7m shares) of Feng Tay, a Taiwanese athletic-footwear maker known as a key Nike supplier. He joined Feng Tay's board as a supervisor in 1997 and was elected a director in 2018; Hurun lists him (under 'China') for his Feng Tay stake.
interesting_fact: Feng Tay's board is notably Nike-linked: fellow director Peter Dale Nickerson is a former general manager of Nike China, and the company describes Chen as versed in its corporate development and risk management after 20+ years on the board.
deep_cut_fact: Outside footwear, he previously served as a supervisor of 綠電再生 (Green Power Recycling / 'Green Electricity Regeneration'), a Taiwanese green-energy/recycling company, per his Feng Tay board bio.
notes: Taiwan-based (Hurun files him under China). Very low public profile, non-executive director. The IR contact is Feng Tay's official spokesperson (Hsu Fang-wei), published on the company's investor page. Name romanised as Chen Shih-jung in Taiwan.

name: Viktor Karachun
current_role: Co-owner, ATB-Market (АТБ-Маркет), Dnipro, Ukraine
profile: Ukrainian businessman (b. 1966, Lypniazhka, Kirovohrad oblast) who is a co-owner of ATB-Market, one of Ukraine's largest retailers (discount grocery chain). ATB was founded in 1993 by Yevhen Yermakov with partners; Karachun joined the ownership in 2000 alongside Hennadiy Butkevych. Forbes Ukraine estimated his wealth at $155m in 2015; Wikidata lists ~$505m.
interesting_fact: ATB-Market was founded in Dnipro in 1993; in 2000 its founding group changed, with Karachun replacing co-founder Serhiy Tarasyuk as a co-owner alongside Yermakov and Butkevych.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the Samarkand Cooperative Institute (Uzbekistan) and first worked in Tajikistan before moving to Dnipropetrovsk, where he later became an ATB co-owner.
notes: Very private. No personal or press contact found on ATB's consumer website (only e-shop addresses). Web search budget ran out for this lane before more checks; current status not independently re-verified for 2026.

name: Gary L. Carano
current_role: Executive Chairman of the Board, Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (Nasdaq: CZR), since July 2020
profile: Reno casino-family executive (age ~64) who ran Eldorado Resorts as CEO and chairman from 2014, then became Executive Chairman of Caesars Entertainment when Eldorado combined with Caesars in July 2020. He is also President of Recreational Enterprises Inc., the family holding company that partly owns G PEG I, operator of six casinos in Reno and Carson City.
interesting_fact: Before leading the public company, he was President and COO of Eldorado Resorts LLC (2004-2014); the Reno family business he helped build ended up acquiring Caesars, the largest US casino operator, with Carano as executive chairman.
deep_cut_fact: He was the General Manager and CEO of Reno's Silver Legacy Resort Casino from its opening in 1995 until September 2014, nearly two decades running a single property before the Caesars era.
notes: Media contact (Kate Whiteley) and IR contact (Brian Agnew) are as published in Caesars' Q3 2026 earnings release (SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1). Carl Icahn's funds secured two board seats in March 2025. He has served on several Nevada charitable boards.

name: Chen Yinhe
current_role: Chairman, General Manager, controlling shareholder and legal representative, Milkyway Intelligent Supply Chain Service Group (密尔克卫, SSE:603713), Shanghai
profile: Born 1974, Chen founded Shanghai Milkyway International Container Freight in 1997 and built it into a leading Chinese chemical-logistics group offering freight forwarding, hazardous-goods warehousing and transport, then chemical distribution and services for the new-energy sector. The company is listed in Shanghai; he remains chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Milkyway specialises in end-to-end supply chains for chemicals, including dangerous-goods warehouses, and has extended into chemical trading and new-energy industry logistics.
deep_cut_fact: He has run the business continuously since founding it in 1997 as a container freight forwarder; his given name 银河 (Yinhe) literally means 'Milky Way', the company's English name.
notes: Relevant to energy (logistics for chemical and new-energy supply chains). Board secretary Miao Leimin; IR email from the 2025 annual report (April 2026).

name: Yu Benhong
current_role: Chairman, Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR:688305), Dalian; member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee
profile: Yu Benhong (b. ~1977) has chaired Kede CNC since 2015; the Dalian company makes five-axis CNC machine tools, high-end CNC systems and key components (servo drives, motors, spindles) aimed at replacing imports, serving aerospace/defence and civil markets. Wealth is shared with Yu Dehai, the founder of the Dalian Guangyang group from which Kede emerged.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of China's few makers of both five-axis machine tools and their own high-end CNC control systems, including blade-machining and blisk centres used for turbine parts.
deep_cut_fact: Before chairing Kede he ran Dalian Guangyang's international industrial-control technology-transfer centre for 16 years (2004-2020); in January 2023 he became a member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee.
notes: Hurun listing shared with Yu Dehai. Relevant to advanced manufacturing/turbine machining. IR email from the 2025 annual report.

name: Gao Shaoyang
current_role: Director and Senior Vice President, Yunnan Botanee Bio-Technology Group (贝泰妮, SZSE:300957), Kunming
profile: Born 1976 and trained in chemical pharmacy, Gao joined Botanee in 2012 and was its executive director and general manager in its early years (2012-2014); he has been a director and senior VP of the listed company since 2024. Botanee owns Winona (薇诺娜), a leading Chinese skincare brand for sensitive skin built on plant actives and a pharmacy-plus-online channel strategy.
interesting_fact: Botanee's Winona brand is focused on sensitive skin, launched through pharmacy/dermatology channels before scaling online; the group also owns Winona Baby, AOXMED and TriPollar.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1999 as a technician at Kunming Dihon Pharmaceutical, later was deputy GM of Shanghai Kangwang cosmetics (2005-2008), then returned to Dihon as a project director before joining Botanee.
notes: Hurun listing shared with Meng Yang. Not the founder/chairman (Guo Zhenyu chairs Botanee). Consumer skincare, not energy. IR email from the 2025 annual report.
